title: 1987 European Parliament election in Portugal
summary: Portugal elected its twenty-four members of the European Parliament for the first time on 19 July 1987, the same day as the legislative election that gave the Social Democrats their absolute majority. The country had acceded on 1 January 1986 and had been represented until then by delegates appointed from the Assembly of the Republic; this ballot filled the remainder of the 1984–1989 term. It is in the atlas as the point at which membership of the Communities became something Portuguese voters were asked about directly, eighteen months after it took effect — and, because the two ballots were held on one day, as an early sign of how little a European election would ever be about Europe here.
